sources_reopened.note: research letter; no abstract in PubMed; 22 of 25 not re-confirmed, relied on record passage

issues.text: In those trials, for every 13 people who took a tablet, about 1 more slept better than with a dummy pill. For every 6, about 1 more had a side effect.
issues.problem: Required qualification missing: the NNT and NNH come from different sets of trials (4 vs 16), the NNT is imprecise and the authors call it a rough guide. Compression makes it read as one head-to-head comparison.
issues.source_says: NNT 13 (95% CI 6.7 to 62.9) from 4 studies; NNH 6 from 16 studies; 'rough guide'.
issues.replacement: As a rough guide from different sets of trials: for every 13 people who took a tablet, about 1 more slept better than with a dummy pill (an imprecise figure); for every 6, about 1 more had a side effect.

issues.text: Sources: https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.38623.768588.47 (Glass 2005) and https://doi.org/10.1111/jgs.18372 (Beers 2023) and https://doi.org/10.1111/jsr.14035 (European Insomnia Guideline)
issues.problem: Visual cites 'ACP 2016' and captions cite US guidelines, but ACP is not in the source reply.
issues.replacement: Sources: https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.38623.768588.47 (Glass 2005), https://doi.org/10.1111/jgs.18372 (Beers 2023), https://doi.org/10.1111/jsr.14035 (European Insomnia Guideline) and https://doi.org/10.7326/M15-2175 (ACP 2016)

issues.text: Sleeping tablets in people aged 60 and over add about 25 minutes of sleep a night, on average.
issues.problem: Present-tense general claim drops 'in short trials' and 'self-reported' from the opening line (they follow later, so minor).
issues.source_says: Mean 25.2 min, self-reported, trials of at least 5 nights.
issues.replacement: In short trials, sleeping tablets in people aged 60 and over added about 25 minutes of self-reported sleep a night, on average.

issues.text: In confirmed cases, about 6 in 100 a year went on to Parkinson's or Lewy body dementia.
issues.problem: Drops the specialist-centre population (and MSA); a short version reads as a general prognosis for people with RBD.
issues.source_says: 1,280 patients with polysomnography-confirmed iRBD at 24 specialist centres; conversion to PD, DLB or MSA 6.3%/year.
issues.replacement: In people with sleep-study-confirmed disease seen at specialist centres, about 6 in 100 a year went on to Parkinson's, Lewy body dementia or a related condition.

issues.text: In 1,280 people with sleep-study-confirmed disease, about 6 in 100 a year developed Parkinson's disease or dementia with Lewy bodies.
issues.problem: Omits specialist-centre setting and multiple system atrophy.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: In 1,280 people with sleep-study-confirmed disease at specialist centres, about 6 in 100 a year developed Parkinson's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies or a related condition.

issues.text: about 3 in 4 by 12 years.
issues.problem: 12-year figure is a Kaplan-Meier estimate with mean follow-up 4.6 years; stated as observed.
issues.source_says: 73.5% converting after 12 years (Kaplan-Meier); average follow-up 4.6 years.
issues.replacement: an estimated 3 in 4 by 12 years.

issues.text: About 6 in 100 a year with confirmed disease developed Parkinson's or Lewy body dementia (specialist centres).
issues.problem: Omits MSA/related conditions.
issues.source_says: PD, DLB and MSA.
issues.replacement: About 6 in 100 a year with confirmed disease developed Parkinson's, Lewy body dementia or a related condition (specialist centres).

issues.text: Older people who had taken benzodiazepines for years were handed a booklet, and many stopped.
issues.problem: 'Handed' asserts in-person delivery (record: say 'given'); 'many' without the number in a headline, and 'for years' is not the trial's definition (long-term users).
issues.source_says: 303 long-term users; 27% vs 5% discontinued at 6 months by pharmacy renewal records.
issues.replacement: Older people on long-term benzodiazepines were given a booklet on the risks with a plan for cutting down, and more stopped: 27 in 100, against 5 in 100 with usual care.

issues.text: Older people who had taken benzodiazepines for years were handed a booklet, and many stopped.
issues.problem: Same as X headline.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: Older people on long-term benzodiazepines were given a booklet on the risks with a plan for cutting down, and more stopped: 27 in 100, against 5 in 100 with usual care.

issues.text: Posting information alone did not reduce use in a large US trial.
issues.problem: Population swap by omission: Singh 2024 mailed materials to people with dementia and their prescribers, across three drug classes.
issues.source_says: 12,787 US health plan members with dementia; mailing to patient and prescriber; dispensing 76.7% vs 77.5% usual care.
issues.replacement: In a large US trial in people with dementia, mailing information to them and their prescribers did not reduce use.

issues.text: Pharmacies ran it, and withdrawal symptoms were common in people who tapered.
issues.problem: Withdrawal figure comes from the second trial (D-PRESCRIBE, 29 of 77 sedative-hypnotic tapers), not the trial described.
issues.source_says: D-PRESCRIBE: 29 of 77 who attempted to taper reported withdrawal symptoms; none hospitalised.
issues.replacement: Pharmacies ran it. In a second trial, about 4 in 10 people who tapered sleeping tablets reported withdrawal symptoms, though none needed hospital care.

issues.text: A vibrating pad woke about 80 in 100; a flashing light, 27 in 100.
issues.problem: Range truncated; also drops 'small' study.
issues.source_says: Bed and pillow shakers woke 80 to 84%.
issues.replacement: In a small lab study... A vibrating pad woke about 80 to 84 in 100; a flashing light, 27 in 100.

issues.text: In an English GP trial, a sleep hygiene booklet was the comparison. Adding four nurse sessions of sleep restriction therapy gave less severe insomnia at 6 months.
issues.problem: Missing required qualification that this was not an older-adult trial (mean age 55); older-adult audience.
issues.source_says: Mean age 55.4 years (range 19 to 88).
issues.replacement: In an English GP trial (mean age 55), a sleep hygiene booklet was the comparison. Adding four nurse sessions of sleep restriction therapy gave less severe insomnia at 6 months.

issues.text: The AASM advises against sleep hygiene alone for long-term insomnia.
issues.problem: Recommendation strength omitted; it is conditional.
issues.source_says: 'We suggest ... not' (CONDITIONAL).
issues.replacement: The AASM suggests not using sleep hygiene alone for long-term insomnia (a conditional recommendation).

issues.text: In older people, gabapentinoids commonly cause sleepiness and dizziness.
issues.problem: Attributes an older-adult-specific frequency claim that neither source makes; AASM reports somnolence and dizziness in trial adults, not older people specifically.
issues.source_says: AASM: 'Adverse effects included somnolence and dizziness.' Guideline does not mention older adults.
issues.replacement: Gabapentinoids commonly cause sleepiness and dizziness.

issues.text: The 2025 US guideline from the American Academy of Sleep Medicine made four changes worth knowing.
issues.problem: Item 3 (aggravators) is a long-standing first step, not a change.
issues.source_says: Good practice statement.
issues.replacement: The 2025 US guideline from the American Academy of Sleep Medicine has four points worth knowing.

issues.text: The guideline now advises against pramipexole, ropinirole or rotigotine as standard, because of augmentation.
issues.problem: Conditional recommendation not stated in X.
issues.source_says: 'suggests against the standard use' (conditional).
issues.replacement: The guideline now suggests not using pramipexole, ropinirole or rotigotine as standard (a conditional recommendation), because of augmentation.

issues.text: advises checking ferritin and transferrin saturation in everyone
issues.problem: Guideline applies to clinically significant RLS.
issues.source_says: 'In all patients with clinically significant RLS'.
issues.replacement: advises checking ferritin and transferrin saturation in everyone with troublesome restless legs

issues.text: The risk over time was about half.
issues.problem: Hazard ratio with wide CI presented as a firm halving in the short version; LinkedIn carries the uncertainty, X does not.
issues.replacement: The risk over time was about half as high with CBT, though the true reduction could be smaller or larger.

issues.text: Broken nights are part of that.
issues.problem: Unsupported causal inference; the source reports a screening count, not that night waking explains daytime sleeping.
issues.source_says: 339 had excessive daytime sleeping; of these, 133 had nighttime sleep disruption and consented.
issues.replacement: Of those, 133 also had broken sleep at night on a wrist monitor and joined the study.

issues.text: Setting checks by each person's skin risk cut waking with no harm to skin.
issues.problem: Overstates: the reduction was in care-related (light/noise) waking, with care by research staff.
issues.source_says: 'Awakenings due to light and sound associated with incontinence care were significantly reduced'.
issues.replacement: Setting checks by each person's skin risk cut care-related waking, with no harm to skin.

issues.text: Checks set by each person's skin risk cut waking without harming skin.
issues.problem: As X.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: Checks set by each person's skin risk cut care-related waking without harming skin.

issues.text: Checks set by each person's skin risk cut waking without harming skin.
issues.problem: As X; also omits small/old US studies.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: In small, older US studies... Checks set by each person's skin risk cut care-related waking without harming skin.

issues.text: In a US trial, phone CBT for insomnia left 56 in 100 older adults free of significant insomnia a year later, against 26 in 100 given information.
issues.problem: Population swap: all participants had osteoarthritis pain; reads as older adults in general.
issues.source_says: 327 adults 60+ with insomnia and OA pain; 67/119 vs 33/128 in remission at 12 months.
issues.replacement: In a US trial of older adults with insomnia and arthritis pain, phone CBT for insomnia left 56 in 100 free of significant insomnia a year later, against 26 in 100 given information.

issues.text: About 1 in 5 people over 60 in England did not use the internet in 2020.
issues.problem: Drops 'living in their own homes' (care home residents excluded).
issues.source_says: ELSA, private households.
issues.replacement: About 1 in 5 people over 60 living at home in England did not use the internet in 2020.

issues.text: CBT for insomnia works by phone
issues.problem: Headline generalises beyond population; fine as RCT but should carry the population on the same card (it does in the kicker). Acceptable; tighten.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: Phone CBT for insomnia helped older adults with arthritis pain

issues.text: In people over 60, sleeping tablets added only about 25 minutes, with more confusion and daytime tiredness.
issues.problem: Missing required qualification that the trials tested nightly use over at least 5 nights, not a single ward dose; also drops 'self-reported' and 'memory problems'.
issues.source_says: C11-02-b qualification: trials were of nightly use over at least 5 nights.
issues.replacement: In trials of nightly use in people over 60, sleeping tablets added only about 25 minutes of reported sleep, with more memory problems, confusion and daytime tiredness.

issues.text: In people over 60, sleeping tablets added only about 25 minutes of sleep, with more confusion and daytime tiredness.
issues.problem: As X.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: In trials of nightly use in people over 60, sleeping tablets added only about 25 minutes of sleep, with more confusion and daytime tiredness.

issues.text: and they slept 83 minutes less than at home.
issues.problem: Self-report of one night; phrased as measured.
issues.source_says: Subjective total sleep time 83 min shorter than habitual sleep at home.
issues.replacement: and they reported sleeping 83 minutes less than at home.

issues.text: Is a diuretic given in the evening? / diuretic in the evening?
issues.problem: Claim C11-02-e has verdict partly_supported; only the Oelke wording (no later than mid to late afternoon) is supported, and only a late-evening or bedtime dose should be named. Current wording stays within that, but the editor should re-grade the claim record to supported_with_qualification limited to the safe wording before publication.
issues.source_says: Oelke 2017: diuretics 'should be taken mid-late afternoon'; Reynard: dose 6 h before bed reduced nocturia.
issues.replacement: Is a diuretic given late in the evening or at bedtime?
